findings.trigger: Two delete requests for the same active donation arrive concurrently (a double click that the frontend does not debounce; waitress serves requests on several threads). Both read the event log at :323-330 before either has written, both compute currently_deleted=False at :346, both pass the guard at :350, and both call progress_service.delete_donation(target_seq) at :358. The comment at :344 says deletion is a toggle in progress_service, so the second call flips the donation back to active. Both requests return success=True with action 'Deleted'. The operator is told twice that the donation was deleted; it is still active and still counted in power and stats.
findings.suggestion: Move the intent check under the same lock progress_service uses for the write (services.mech.progress_service.LOCK, which reset.py already imports for exactly this reason), or give progress_service.delete_donation an explicit desired state ('delete'/'restore') so that a toggle that does not match the intent is refused inside the locked section rather than before it. SPEC B4 says ':299 blocks the stale double click' - it blocks the sequential one, not the simultaneous one.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether the browser disables the button after the first click, whether the web route serialises these POSTs, or whether progress_service.delete_donation re-checks the state itself under its lock. If any of those holds, this cannot happen.

findings.trigger: Inside the lock the reset runs backup -> clear event log -> reset seq counter -> write fresh snapshot. If _reset_sequence_counter (:55) or _write_fresh_snapshot (:56) raises (disk full, read-only data dir, a corrupt old snapshot making _previous_member_count irrelevant but progress_service helpers raising OSError), the handler at :78 returns success=False 'File I/O error' - but the event log has already been truncated at :54. The ledger is now empty while the live snapshot still shows the old power and level (or the seq counter is 0 while the snapshot is old). The operator sees 'reset failed', reads the mech state, and it still looks intact; the next donation is booked with seq 1 on top of a snapshot built from events that no longer exist. Z1 holds (the backup exists), but the reported result and the actual state disagree.
findings.suggestion: Prepare the new snapshot and seq file as temp files BEFORE truncating the event log and only then truncate + os.replace both, so the irreversible step is last; or on any exception after _clear_event_log, restore event log/seq/snapshots from the backup directory just created and say so in the error message.

findings.trigger: new_state = mech_service.get_state() is read at :58 and only afterwards clear_mech_cache() runs at :60, although processors.clear_mech_cache's own docstring says the cache is cleared 'before emitting events' and the reset just rewrote the files behind it. If mech_service.get_state() is served from the MechDataStore cache, new_state equals old_state: emit_reset_event then carries old_power == new_power and level_changed=False, and the DonationResult handed to the panel reports the pre-reset power as the new power - 'reset done, power still 1234'.
findings.suggestion: Call clear_mech_cache() before the second get_state() (directly after the with-block), not after it.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether mech_service.get_state() reads through the MechDataStore cache or straight from the snapshot files. If it reads the files, the order is harmless.

findings.trigger: _usable and _cents were added (docstrings :40-51, :61-65) because one odd ledger line took the whole history page down. The same class of line still does: an event with "payload": null passes _usable (seq is fine), then payload.get('donor', ...) at :160 / :170 / :186 / :198 raises AttributeError on None; a PowerGiftGranted with "campaign_id": null raises at :172 (None.lower()). Both land in the (KeyError, ValueError, AttributeError) handler at :290 and the entire history returns success=False - the delete and restore buttons, the only way to repair the ledger from the panel, disappear with it. delete_donation already guards the same access with (event.get('payload') or {}) at :328 and :340; get_donation_stats has the same hole at :442. Two readers of the same file, hardened to different degrees.
findings.suggestion: Read payload as (event.get('payload') or {}) in get_donation_history and get_donation_stats as delete_donation does, and coerce campaign_id with str(... or ''). Better: make _usable also demand a dict payload and skip the line with the same warning.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see the writer (progress_service). If it can never emit payload=null or campaign_id=null, only a hand edit or an older schema triggers this - which is exactly the case the existing hardening was written for.

findings.trigger: Only successful attempts append to response_times (:114-115); a timed-out attempt records nothing but a failure count. Container fast for 20 polls (500 ms) -> get_adaptive_timeout = max(1000, 750, 10000) = 10000 ms. The container then becomes slow (needs 15 s, e.g. a game server under load). Every poll times out at 10 s, none succeeds, so response_times never changes; after enough failures success_rate < 0.8 gives 15000 ms at :161 - and there it stays for good, because the profile can only learn from a success and a success needs a longer timeout than it will ever grant. success_rate is cumulative over total_attempts and never windowed, so it cannot recover either. The container is reported as failing on every poll although the initial 45 s cap would have reached it.
findings.suggestion: Record the timeout duration as an observation on failure (or bump max_response_time to the timeout that expired), and window success_rate over the same history_window as response_times, so the timeout can grow back toward max_timeout after a run of failures.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see the caller of get_adaptive_timeout: if the fetch service retries with a longer timeout on failure, or does not use the adaptive value at all, the stuck state does not occur.

findings.trigger: get_donation_history and get_donation_stats both call mech_service.get_mech_state_service and return failure if it fails (:122-128, :411-416). The result is then never used: MechStateCompat at :130-135 is built and never read again, and the stats method drops mech_state_result entirely - every number comes from the event log. So a mech-state failure (corrupt snapshot, member-count or decay maths raising) turns the ledger view into 'Failed to get mech state' although the event log itself is readable - and this page is the only way to repair the ledger from the panel (see _usable docstring). In the case where the operator most needs the history, a dependency it does not need takes it away.
findings.suggestion: Drop the mech state call and MechStateCompat from both methods, or downgrade the failed mech-state to a logged warning and still return the ledger.
findings.unsure_why: The gate may be intentional as a health check; but no comment says so and the fetched value is demonstrably unused.

findings.trigger: from_dict writes the parsed datetime back into the caller's dict (data['last_updated'] = datetime.fromisoformat(...)). A caller that keeps the dict (a JSON cache it later dumps again, or one that calls from_dict twice on the same dict) gets a TypeError: json.dump cannot serialise datetime, and the second from_dict passes a datetime to fromisoformat.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether from_dict has any caller at all.

findings.trigger: _create_default_config's comment says the values 'come from DDC_FAST_STATS_TIMEOUT and DDC_FAST_INFO_TIMEOUT' and the INFO log says 'Performance config aligned with Docker timeouts' - but both values are the literal 45.0; no environment variable is read and the try/except at :46-71 guards pure arithmetic that cannot raise. An operator who raises DDC_FAST_INFO_TIMEOUT to 90 s for a slow host still gets adaptive timeouts capped at 45 s, and the log tells them the opposite.
findings.suggestion: Either read the two environment variables (with 45.0 as fallback) or reword comment and log to say the cap is fixed at 45 s.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether those environment variables still exist anywhere else in the project or whether the adaptive timeout is used by any caller.

notes: F3 concerns reset_donations as well (one verdict slot, so it is listed only in findings). F4 also touches get_donation_stats at :442 (event.get('payload', {}).get('deleted_seq') on a null payload). Observations without a statable trigger: (1) CachedStatus.is_expired/age_seconds subtract cached_at from an aware datetime.now(timezone.utc); if StatusCacheService (not visible) stores a naive datetime, every cache read raises TypeError. (2) get_donation_history and get_donation_stats compute the same parity/total in two hand-written copies; they agree today (both use odd-count = deleted) but can drift; and both compute 'currently deleted' independently of how progress_service rebuilds, which I cannot see. (3) DonationStats.from_data is called by neither method in this file; if an outside caller passes the display list (which contains deletion rows), the count would include them. (4) delete_donation and the history reader treat deleted_seq only by truthiness; a string '5' would be tracked under a different key than int 5 and silently make the donation look active. (5) compute_unique_member_count in unified/member_count.py is async but calls the member-count service synchronously; if that service method is a coroutine function, callers get an un-awaited coroutine instead of an int - cannot see the service. (6) reset.py rewrites only the 'main' snapshot; other snapshots in snapshot_dir, if any, would survive the reset with no events behind them. (7) _backup_before_reset copies snapshot_dir into data_dir/backup_x; if snapshot_dir is data_dir itself the copytree would include the backup directory being written - depends on ProgressPaths, not visible. (8) notification_service deletes a file that fails to parse; if donation_service.py writes it non-atomically, a read mid-write loses an announcement - Z8-visible via the error log, not silent. (9) classify_containers comment says 'no successful attempts' while the code tests total_attempts == 0; a container with only failures is classified slow via is_slow/success_rate, so the outcome is the same. (10) performance_service.get_all_profiles returns a shallow copy: the PerformanceProfile objects inside are shared and mutable.
